status_summary: On 2026-09-17 the SEC issued an Innovation Exemption order giving temporary, conditional exemptions for five years to venues trading tokenized stocks and to liquidity providers, which the Chairman's statement ties to the Exchange Act general exemptive authority in section 36(a)(1); it relieves trading venues rather than issuers. On 2026-08-21 the SEC published proposed Regulation Crypto Assets (91 FR 54510), with issuer offering exemptions of $5 million over four years and $75 million per 12 months, comments due 2026-10-20. The issuer-focused step is a proposal, and no measure showing more frequent use of exemptive authority was found.

timeline.event: The SEC publishes the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets (91 FR 54510, File No. S7-2026-27), with offering exemptions of $5 million over four years and $75 million per 12 months and a conditional safe harbor; comments are due 2026-10-20.

The SEC issues an order under Exchange Act section 36(a)(1) granting temporary, conditional exemptions from the exchange and dealer definitions for tokenized securities venues and liquidity providers, expiring five years after publication, and invites comment.

title: Use SEC general exemptive authority more often to reduce burdens on issuers
uncertainties: The Chairman's 2026-09-17 statement was re-read in this review on sec.gov; it cites Exchange Act section 36(a)(1) for exemptions to tokenized securities venues and liquidity providers, gives issuers only a right to object, and does not state a term, so the five-year duration rests on the SEC press release as read by the researcher. The Federal Register record of Regulation Crypto Assets was re-read in this review for its first 100,000 of 122,991 characters, confirming 91 FR 54510, File No. S7-2026-27 and the 2026-10-20 comment deadline; the statutory authority section was not reached, so whether its exemptions rest on Securities Act section 28 is unconfirmed. Exemptive orders issued in 2025 were not itemized; a March 2025 law-firm note describing several orders was paywalled. A Federal Register API query was refused for URL length, so SEC exemptive orders published after 2026-09-01 were not enumerated. Earlier announcements that an innovation exemption was planned are statements, not events. The limb on markedly more frequent use of exemptive authority rests on absence of evidence.
